# WHO African Region Mpox Bulletin - 11 August 2024

Format
:   Analysis

Source
:   * [WHO](/organization/who)

Posted


Originally published


Origin
:   [View original](https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/378456)

## Attachments

* [![Preview of AFRO-Mpox bulletin -11 August 2024.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/7e/13/7e13795a-888c-4ebd-a7b3-c5d6a83c3d4f.png?2557348-1-0)  **Download Report** (PDF | 1.12 MB)](/attachments/7e13795a-888c-4ebd-a7b3-c5d6a83c3d4f/AFRO-Mpox%20bulletin%20-11%20August%202024.pdf)

**Overview**

Since the beginning of 2024, the number of laboratory-confirmed mpox cases and deaths reported to the WHO Regional Office for Africa (AFRO) as of 07 August 2024 was 2,081 and 13, respectively, with a case fatality ratio (CFR) of 0.6%. The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), due to its large number of cases, remains a significant focus for ongoing monitoring and response efforts. The 13 confirmed deaths were reported from three countries (DRC = 8, South Africa = 3 and Cameroon = 2).

In 2024, 15 countries in the AFRO region reported mpox cases as of 07 August 2024, five of which reported cases for the first time (Burundi = 61, Côte d’Ivoire = 7, Kenya = 1, Rwanda = 4, Uganda = 2). DRC continues to account for the highest proportion of reported cases (98.8%). As of 07 August 2024, DRC reported 1888 confirmed cases. In 2024, the DRC confirmed an outbreak linked to limited testing access in rural areas.

Burundi declared the mpox epidemic on 25 July 2024. As of 07 August 2024, suspected cases have been reported in 17 out of the 49 districts, spanning across 11 health provinces. Each of these 17 health districts has confirmed at least one case of Mpox, but no deaths have been reported. The cumulative number of confirmed mpox cases as of 7 August is 61\*, with males accounting for 52.5% and females for 47.5%. So far, a total of 406 contacts have been traced for these confirmed cases and are currently being monitored within the community. Among the confirmed cases, children under the age of five make up 26.2%, followed by individuals aged between 31 to 40 years (24.6%) and those aged between 11 to 20 years (19.7%).

Cameroon reported a total of 5 laboratory-confirmed mpox cases and 2 deaths, with a high CFR of 40.0% from January to April 2024. Since the beginning of the mpox outbreak in 2022, Cameroon has reported 50 cases and 5 deaths with a CFR of 10.0%.

In the Central African Republic (CAR), there were 28 reported laboratory-confirmed cases of mpox from January to August 2024 across 6 health regions, with zero deaths. Since 2022, CAR has reported 75 laboratory-confirmed cases and 1 death (CFR = 1.3%).

In Congo, 19 mpox cases were reported with no associated deaths from January to April 2024. However, the country has reported 45 laboratory-confirmed cases and 2 deaths since the beginning of the outbreak in 2022 (CFR = 4.4%).

In Côte d’Ivoire, As of August 7, 2024, a total of 7 cases of mpox have been reported across three health districts: Tabou (1 case), Koumassi (1 case), and Yopougon-Ouest-Songon (5 cases). Fortunately, there have been no deaths associated with these cases. Out of the 7 confirmed cases, 4 (57%) cases are males, and all seven individuals affected are above the age of 15. Currently, 40 contacts have been identified and are being closely monitored. However, the exact transmission chain for these cases has not yet been definitively determined.

In the DRC, there have been a cumulative total of 14,091 suspected cases of mpox and 511 deaths (CFR =3.6%) from January to 07 August 2024. Of the 14,091 suspected cases, 1,888† have been laboratory confirmed. Over the past eight weeks, there has been an overall increasing trend in suspected cases, indicating a growing concern for public health authorities in the region. The DRC reported a significantly higher number of laboratory-confirmed mpox cases, with 1,888 cases and 8 deaths, with a CFR of 0.4% since the beginning of 2024.

The DRC’s mpox outbreak is concentrated in a few key provinces, with Equateur bearing the brunt of the cases and deaths, followed by South Kivu. The significant increase in suspected cases over the past eight weeks across the country underscores the urgent need for enhanced public health measures.

Rwanda reported 4 mpox cases, with 11 contacts being traced as of 27 July 2024 (City of Kigali (COK) =3; and Rusizi =1). The case reported on 27 July was a 39-year-old male Rwandan, working with an international NGO in Kigali, a resident of Kicukiro, Kanombe, now selfisolated in Kimironko. No recent travel history and no contact with a confirmed or suspected mpox case.

South Africa reported 24 cases of mpox, with 3 deaths (CFR = 13.6%) between April and August 2024, indicating a substantial fatality rate among the reported cases.

Kenya reported its first case of mpox on 29 July 2024. The case was confirmed by the Ministry of Health in Taita Taveta County, located on the Kenya-Tanzania border. The patient is a 42- year-old Kenyan male, a long-distance truck driver residing in the Kinoo area of Kiambu County, which is adjacent to Nairobi. He had traveled from Kampala, Uganda, to Mombasa on 12 July 2024, using the main A104 corridor (Kampala-Malaba-Eldoret-Nakuru-NairobiMombasa). At the time of identification, he was en route to Rwanda through Tanzania via the Taveta One Stop Border Point. A total of 12 suspected cases were identified, with one case testing positive for MPXV Clade Ib. No deaths had been reported as of 11 August 2024.

This update includes specific insights into the mpox situation in South Africa and the DRC, emphasising the ongoing need for improved preparedness, surveillance, and response measures to manage and mitigate the impact of mpox in the region.

All rights reserved. | Page 1 Summary The mpox virus is classiﬁed into 2 main clades, clade I and clade II, with each further subdivided into clade Ia, the newly identiﬁed clade Ib, clade IIa, and clade IIb, the clade which was responsible for the 2022 global outbreak. Since the 2022 clade IIb mpox outbreak began, there have more than 115,101 cases and more than 255 deaths reported in 126 countries, though world-wide reported data likely do not include the most recent outbreaks of clade I in the Africa region. According to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (US CDC) and the World Health Organization (WHO), the US has reported 34,187 mpox cases as of October 31, 2024. The US outbreak has continued to grow at a low but steady pace in 2024, with 2,501 cases recorded year to date as of November 23, 2024. With the continued transmission of clade IIb in the US and globally and the increased transmission of clade I and II in the Africa region, experts are concerned that changes in the national and global landscape have the potential to increase health risks for speciﬁc US populations. Mov. Avg. (Mpox Cases) Situation Update: December 3, 2024 Mpox Virus: Clade I and Clade II ©2024 The Johns Hopkins University. All rights reserved. | Page 2 Key Updates Global Response • The UN authorized KM Biologics LC16 vaccine for children >1 year old on November 20, 2024. • The WHO extended their PHEIC declaration for mpox on November 22, 2024. • The WHO added the Japanese KM Biologics LC16 vaccine to its emergency use authorization list, making it the second vaccine to be approved for mpox prevention. • Vaccination campaigns continue to be delayed, notably in the DRC, as coordination efforts stall. As of October, only 20% of the doses provided to the DRC have been administered and children > 12 in the DRC are still not eligible for vaccination. o Nigeria’s campaign began administering vaccines on November 18, 2024, more than three weeks after the initiative was slated to start. • Africa CDC approved the ﬁrst mpox diagnostic tool that is manufactured on the continent, a real-time PCR test developed in Morocco. • The WHO approved two new mpox diagnostic tests for emergency use on October 30, 2024. • The WHO approved the age extension authorization for the prequaliﬁed MVA-BN vaccine to include children ages 12-17, per the European Medicines Agency recommendation. Both Clades • Angola’s Ministry of Health conﬁrmed their ﬁrst case of mpox (clade unknown) on November 16, 2024. • Mauritius announced their ﬁrst case of mpox (clade unknown) on October 27, 2024. • There are multiple new and ongoing outbreaks of mpox clades Ia, Ib, and IIb across Africa. As of November 18, 2024, a total of 55,413 cases (12,162 conﬁrmed) and 1,142 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] of 2.1%) were reported from 20 African Union Member States. DRC accounts for about 80% of cases and deaths. Clade I • Cases in the DRC have begun to plateau, while case detection in Burundi continues to rise. Experts expect cases to plateau or drop globally in the coming months. • The UK conﬁrmed that a ﬁfth individual was diagnosed with clade Ib mpox. The four other cases originated from a housemate with a recent travel history to Uganda. • Canada detected their ﬁrst case of clade Ib mpox in an individual with a recent travel history on November 22, 2024. • On November 16, 2024, the ﬁrst case of clade Ib mpox was detected in the US, which had previously only detected clade II cases. The individual was diagnosed in California after recent travel to West Africa. • The UK detected their ﬁrst case of clade Ib mpox on October 30, 2024 in an individual with a recent travel history. 4 new cases were reported on November 9, 2024. Situation Update: December 3, 2024 Mpox Virus: Clade I and Clade II ©2024 The Johns Hopkins University. All rights reserved. | Page 3 • Increases in clade I cases continue to be documented across the African Continent (see details on country-speciﬁc case and death counts below). • Since the beginning of the year, DRC has recorded more than 48,000 conﬁrmed or suspected cases, with over 1,100 deaths (see detailed DRC section below). • The likelihood that cases of clade I will be imported to the US has increased in recent weeks as cases have begun to be detected in countries outside of the Africa region. Clade II • A MMWR from October 10, 2024 discussed a second cluster of mpox cases in the US that were caused tecovirimat-resistant monkeypox virus. For more information about speciﬁc mpox scenarios and health risks, see the CORI Mpox Resource Page. Background The monkeypox (mpox) virus—a serious viral zoonosis endemic in west and central Africa—is classiﬁed into 2 main clades, clade I and clade II, with each further subdivided into clade Ia, the newly identiﬁed clade Ib, clade IIa, and clade IIb. Clade I mpox is generally associated with higher CFRs (1.4% to ~10%) compared with clade II (0.1% to 3.6%). In 2022, the epidemiology of clade IIb mpox shifted dramatically. The virus, which is historically transmitted through close contact with infected wildlife or infected persons, found a foothold in the sexual networks of gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men, including in the United States and Europe. Although the clade IIb virus is capable of transmission via respiratory droplets, short-range aerosols, or contact with contaminated objects (fomite transmission), the majority of cases from the global epidemic were acquired through close, extended physical contact, particularly intimate or sexual contact. The change in epidemiology and rapid spread of the virus in 2022 required urgent public health action, and WHO declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) on July 23, 2022. Public health officials and community-based organizations in the US and worldwide mounted a response that included health education, awareness raising, testing, treatment, and vaccination with a vaccine that was originally designed to protect against smallpox but is also effective against mpox. By late summer, the public health response began to slow transmission. Vaccination campaigns and targeted interventions signiﬁcantly reduced the number of new weekly cases. However, cases continue to occur among individuals at increased risk of infection, particularly those who have not been vaccinated or have received only 1 dose of the 2-dose vaccine. Situation Update: December 3, 2024 Mpox Virus: Clade I and Clade II ©2024 The Johns Hopkins University. All rights reserved. | Page 4 In 2024, the DRC has experienced an unprecedented number of clade I mpox cases, with transboundary cases occurring in several neighboring countries. Additionally, a new offshoot of clade I has emerged, called clade Ib, that may be causing more severe disease. Before April 2023, there were no formally documented cases of sexual transmission of clade I mpox, but many clusters of sexual transmission have since been recorded in the DRC. Notably, 4.3%–5.7% of all suspected and conﬁrmed clade I cases in DRC reported from January 1, 2023, to April 14, 2024, have been fatal. Additionally, 67% of all cases and 78% of deaths have occurred among children aged 15 years and younger. This new mode of sexual transmission, as well as other possible modes of transmission, and newly or more severely affected groups such as heterosexual sex workers and children, raise additional concerns over the continuing rapid expansion of the DRC outbreak. Key Public Health Recommendations To minimize the health impact of mpox in the US, CDC and WHO recommend the following for clinicians and health departments: • Implement prevention strategies: o Recommend all adults at an elevated risk of infection and those planning travel to affected countries receive 2 doses of JYNNEOS vaccine administered 28 days apart. o Mass gathering event planning and preparedness activities should foster community-based actions aimed at spreading precise and practical public health advice with a nondiscriminatory approach, utilizing different media and incorporate educational and awareness-raising initiatives related to mpox and other diseases of concern. • Consider mpox as a potential diagnosis: o In patients with consistent symptoms and epidemiological risk factors, including those with recent travel to DRC or neighboring countries or contact with symptomatic individuals from affected areas. o In vaccinated individuals or those previously diagnosed with mpox. • Implement proper infection control and patient management: o Follow CDC guidance on infection prevention and control to minimize transmission risk. o Advise suspected cases to isolate from others and counsel on preventing household transmission through disinfection practices. o Consult health departments or CDC for severe cases, especially those with advanced HIV. • Ensure thorough laboratory testing: o Evaluate all suspected cases with laboratory testing, not only clinical diagnosis. o Follow specimen collection guidelines and send specimens to appropriate state or commercial laboratories. Situation Update: December 3, 2024 Mpox Virus: Clade I and Clade II ©2024 The Johns Hopkins University. All rights reserved. | Page 5 Available Medical Countermeasures While clades I and II mpox viruses are genetically similar enough that vaccines and treatments are expected to be effective, it is not well understood how prior infection with clade IIb (responsible for the ongoing global outbreak) or vaccination might protect from infection with or complications from clade I. CDC recommends that all individuals with an elevated risk of infection receive 2 doses of JYNNEOS vaccine for the best protection against both clades I and II. The DRC National Regulatory Authority recently authorized 2 vaccines for emergency use, MVA-BN (brand name JYNNEOS in the US) and LC16 (Japan). As part of its standing recommendations, WHO advises countries to make vaccines available to nations in need. In March 2024, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued Emergency Use Authorizations (EUAs) for an in vitro mpox diagnostic device and an mpox home test collection kit. Current Global Response World Health Organization The WHO added the MVA-BN vaccine to its prequaliﬁcation list on September 13, 2024, which will allow speedier procurement and country-based approval processes of the Bavarian Nordic vaccine. On November 19, 2024, Japan’s KM Biologics vaccine LC16 was granted emergency use authorization by the WHO as well. On August 14, 2024 the World Health Organization (WHO) declared the current outbreaks of multiple clades of mpox in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), and nearby countries in Africa, to be a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). The PHEIC declaration was extended on November 22, 2024. WHO also: • Elevated the global mpox outbreak to an acute Grade 3 emergency in accordance with the WHO Emergency Response Framework and issued guidance to WHO Member States. • Released funds from its Contingency Fund for Emergencies (CFE), developed a US$15 million regional response plan, and authorized an additional US$1 million of emergency funding to boost response efforts. • Extended for an additional year the WHO Director General’s Standing Recommendations for mpox ﬁrst issued on August 21, 2023. • Began the process for Emergency Use Listing for 2 mpox vaccines to ease access and distribution processes, including distribution aid from GAVI and UNICEF. Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) Africa CDC declared this outbreak to be a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS), signaling the increased threat of international spread posed by this virus. A large driver of these declarations is the spread of clade Ib. Situation Update: December 3, 2024 Mpox Virus: Clade I and Clade II ©2024 The Johns Hopkins University. All rights reserved. | Page 6 European Union (EU) The EU announced that they aim to deliver 566,000 doses of Bavarian Nordic mpox vaccine to affected countries throughout Africa. The first batch of 99,000 doses arrived in the DRC on September 6, 2024, and more are routed for Burundi. GAVI GAVI announced on September 18, 2024, that they will purchase, transport, deliver, and administer 500,000 doses of the Bavarian Nordic vaccine across Africa. Global Fund The Global Fund announced on September 18, 2024 that it will be supporting the DRC’s efforts to combat mpox with $9.5 million in emergency funds. Contributions include enhancing surveillance systems, boosting laboratory capacity, risk communication, infection prevention and control measures, supporting country-level coordination efforts, and strengthening health facility capacity. United States 50,000 doses of US-donated JYNNEOS vaccine arrived in DRC on September 10, 2024. Profiles for Countries with Recent Outbreaks United States (Clade IIb Outbreak) Until November 16, 2024, all mpox cases reported within the US were of the clade IIb subtype. The ﬁrst clade Ib case was detected in an individual in California with a recent travel history to West Africa. There are no other reported cases of clade Ib circulating in the US. Since 2022, the US outbreak has grown to more than 34,187 cases and 63 deaths. Recorded numbers of mpox cases were relatively stable in the ranges of 60-80 news cases per week in the ﬁrst half of the year before dropping off and leveling out at 10-15 cases per week after the summer (see Epi curve on Page 1 for details). High levels of immunity from prior infections and vaccination help mitigate the risk of large outbreaks. Individuals at highest risk for clade IIb infection are gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men; people with multiple sexual partners; sex workers; and healthcare workers caring for infected patients. Democratic Republic of the Congo (Clade I Outbreak) The DRC government declared a national epidemic in December 2022 for what is the largest surge in mpox cases ever recorded in the country. Since the beginning of this year and as of November 3, 2024, WHO has reported 48,163 cases of clade I mpox (8,662 conﬁrmed) and 1,146 deaths in DRC, for a CFR of 2.4%. Based on the extent of the DRC outbreak, in combination with the demographic characteristics and the genetic diversity of cases, experts suspect that multiple transmission factors are driving the outbreak, including zoonotic, household, and sexual. Situation Update: December 3, 2024 Mpox Virus: Clade I and Clade II ©2024 The Johns Hopkins University. All rights reserved. | Page 7 The current DRC clade I outbreak is widespread, affecting all of the country’s 26 provinces, including the capital city of Kinshasa. The highest transmission rates have been in Equateur and Sud-Kivu. The province of Equateur remains the epicenter, contributing more than half of the country's suspected cases and three-quarters of deaths in 2024 alone. The clade I outbreak has mostly affected children, with 66% of cases and 82% of deaths among individuals ages 15 and younger. Experts believe this is likely because younger children were never vaccinated against the related smallpox virus; vaccination was discontinued shortly after smallpox was eradicated in 1980. Many children in the region also suffer from malnutrition, making it more difficult for their bodies to ﬁght infection. Notably, a new more dangerous strain of clade I mpox virus was documented in June 2024 in Sud-Kivu, described as an outbreak having pandemic potential that warrants urgent public health and case management support and targeted vaccination. However, vaccines are so far unavailable in the DRC, although their distribution and use has been authorized. According to experts, the clade Ib infections in DRC are being transmitted through sexual contact, particularly among sex workers and their contacts, as well as household and direct contact, and presenting with whole body or genital lesions that last longer than clade IIb symptoms. The more severe cases have a mortality rate near 5% in adults and 10% in children and have been associated with pregnancy loss. Other cases and clusters of mpox have been reported in Africa, Asia, and Europe in 2024, including: Africa Angola (Unknown Clade Outbreak) On November 16, 2024, the Angola Ministry of Health confirmed their first case of mpox, detected in an individual from the DRC. Clade-specific test results and travel history details are not yet available. Burundi (Clade Ib Outbreak) On July 25, 2024, the Burundi Ministry of Health and Africa CDC reported the first-ever cases of mpox in the country, with 3 confirmed cases. By November 18, 2024, there have been 3,864 confirmed or suspected cases and no deaths. Children <15 account for 48% of the cases. Cameroon (Clade II Outbreak) Since the beginning of 2024, Cameroon has recorded 111 confirmed and suspected mpox cases and 2 deaths. Children under 15 years of age account for 60% of all confirmed cases. CAR (Clade Ia Outbreak) Since the start of the year, CAR has detected 403 confirmed and suspected clade Ia mpox cases and two deaths across 6 of its 10 regions. Of the confirmed cases, children <15 years of age account for 53% of the cases. Situation Update: December 3, 2024 Mpox Virus: Clade I and Clade II ©2024 The Johns Hopkins University. All rights reserved. | Page 8 Cote d’Ivoire (Clade IIa Outbreak) As of August 16, 2024, the Cote d’Ivoire reported 2 confirmed mpox cases and activated its emergency health system in response. Africa CDC reports on November 18, 2024 a total of 412 confirmed or suspected cases and one death due to clade II mpox. Gabon (Clade Ia Outbreak) On August 22, 2024, the Gabon Ministry of Health confirmed a case of mpox in an individual with travel history to Uganda. By October 26, 2024, Africa CDC reports 24 cases and no deaths. Ghana (Clade IIb Outbreak) On October 2, 2024, Ghana reported their first confirmed mpox case of the year to Africa CDC. The case was detected in a 15-year-old male with no travel or sexual history. Since the beginning of the year, there have been 230 suspected cases, two of which have been confirmed and no deaths. Guinea (Unknown Clade Outbreak) On September 3, 2024, the Guinea National Agency for Health Security reported 1 confirmed case and 23 suspected cases, the first outbreak since 2022. The confirmed case had no history of recent travel. There currently is no available clade-specific data. As of September 30, 2024, Africa CDC reports 41 cases (1 confirmed). Kenya (Clade Ib Outbreak) On July 31, 2024, the Kenyan Ministry of Health announced a case of mpox linked to an individual who traveled from Uganda to Rwanda via Kenya. As of November 18, 2024, Africa CDC reports 17 confirmed cases and one death. Liberia (Clade II Outbreak) Since the beginning of the year, Liberia has detected 8 confirmed and 85 suspected mpox cases and no deaths. WHO reports that the outbreak is clade II. Africa CDC reports a total of 315 suspected or confirmed cases and no deaths as of November 18, 2024. 41% of cases are children <15 years of age. Mauritius (Unknown Clade Outbreak) The Mauritius Ministry of Health reported their first case of mpox (clade unknown) on October 27, 2024. The case was detected in an individual who had recently traveled to Kenya. Morocco (Clade IIb Outbreak) On September 12, 2024, Morocco reported their first case of mpox. Africa CDC released an updated outbreak report as cases of mpox continue to expand within the continent and have now reached all 5 regions. Situation Update: December 3, 2024 Mpox Virus: Clade I and Clade II ©2024 The Johns Hopkins University. All rights reserved. | Page 9 Nigeria (Clade IIb Outbreak) On October 21, 2024 Nigeria has reported 1,297 cases (94 laboratory confirmed) of clade II mpox and no deaths for the year to date Republic of the Congo (ROC) (Clade Ia Outbreak) ROC has recorded 162 confirmed and suspected cases of clade I mpox and 1 death since the beginning of the year. On November 3, 2024, Africa CDC reported a total of 249 cases (22 confirmed) and no deaths. Children under 15 years of age account for 38% of all cases. Rwanda (Clade Ib Outbreak) The Rwandan Ministry of Health reported 4 confirmed cases of clade Ia mpox WHO confirmed that the subclade is clade Ib. South Africa (Clade IIb Outbreak) In May 2024, South Africa announced its ﬁrst conﬁrmed case of mpox clade IIb. By September 9, 2024, South Africa has reported 25 conﬁrmed cases and 3 deaths. The cases are all male, aged between 17-43 years, almost all self-identiﬁed as MSM, most are living with HIV, and many displayed severe clinical presentation and were hospitalized for mpox. Of 5 cases with available viral sequence data, all were conﬁrmed to be clade IIb. Uganda (Clade Ib Outbreak) On August 3, 2024, Uganda reported its first 2 cases of mpox ever in people who had crossed the border into DRC. WHO confirmed the cases were clade Ib. As of November 18, 2024, there are a total of 443 confirmed cases and one death of clade Ib mpox. Zambia (Unknown Clade Outbreak) On October 10, 2024. the Zambian Ministry of Health confirmed the first case of mpox in a 32-year old male Tanzanian truck driver. There is no clade-specific data currently available. Zimbabwe (Unknown Clade Outbreak) The Zimbabwe Ministry of Health declared their first case of mpox on October 13, 2024, detected in an 11-year-old male with a recent travel history. By October 21, 2024, there have been 2 cases and no deaths. There is no clade-specific information available currently. Europe UK (Clade Ib Outbreak) The UK Health Security Administration announced on October 30, 2024. that they had detected their ﬁrst case of clade Ib mpox in an individual with a recent travel history. On November 9, 2024, 4 total cases were reported, all housemates. On December 1, 2024, a ﬁfth case was reported, the ﬁrst case that is not connected to the individual who had returned from Uganda in early November. Situation Update: December 3, 2024 Mpox Virus: Clade I and Clade II ©2024 The Johns Hopkins University. All rights reserved. | Page 10 North America Canada (clade Ib Outbreak) On November 22, 2024, the Public Health Agency of Canada announced that the first case of clade Ib mpox was detected in an individual who had recently traveled to a country in Africa with a current mpox outbreak. warnings: PHEIC CONTEXT: WHO declared mpox a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on 14 August 2024, driven substantially by the DRC clade Ib outbreak — expect elevated reporting volume, potential data revisions, and multiple overlapping sitreps during this window

CLADE SPECIFICITY: DRC August 2024 data involves both endemic clade I and the newly characterized clade Ib (associated with sexual transmission networks in eastern DRC, particularly South Kivu) — distinguish clade when reported
DATA COMPLETENESS: DRC surveillance infrastructure is resource-constrained; significant underreporting is expected, especially at health-zone and community levels
LANGUAGE: Primary official DRC sources are in French — query terms and source reading must accommodate French-language content ('cas', 'décès', 'flambée', 'bulletin épidémiologique', etc.)
TEMPORAL OVERLAP: August 2024 data may appear in reports dated September or October 2024 (retrospective sitreps) — do not restrict source search strictly to August publication dates

EXTRACTION MODEL WARNING (from task_input_warnings): extraction_record_model_still_hantavirus_named — verify that the extraction schema in use has been updated to Mpox-appropriate field names before ingestion; do not allow Hantavirus-specific fields to contaminate Mpox records

SOURCE DISCOVERY WARNING (from task_input_warnings): source_discovery_not_yet_disease_generic — source discovery pipeline may not yet be fully generalized; manually verify that Mpox-specific source categories (WHO DON, Africa CDC, INRB, DRC MoH) are included in the discovery scope
DOUBLE-COUNTING RISK: WHO, Africa CDC, and DRC MoH may report the same underlying data — cross-reference source chains and avoid double-counting when aggregating
SUBNATIONAL GRANULARITY: Prioritize province-level and health-zone-level data; national aggregates alone are insufficient for this collection task
EVIDENCE QUOTE REQUIREMENT: Every extracted record must include a verbatim evidence_quote from the source document supporting the numeric values recorded

selection_manifest.human_review_reason: The ECDC is a highly authoritative international public health body (authority_score=0.95), and this report is directly disease-relevant (disease_relevance_score=0.95) and timely (timeliness_score=0.95) for the August 2024 Mpox/clade I window. However, the deterministic model correctly penalizes this source on local and geographic granularity grounds (local_relevance_score=0.58; geographic_granularity_score=0.58): ECDC epidemiological updates on DRC Mpox are produced from a European surveillance perspective and typically aggregate or summarize DRC data rather than originating it. The source is therefore best suited to a 'context' role rather than primary 'collection'. The role_hint was 'collection' but both the deterministic role assignment and the source_role_final converge on 'context', and the 'screening_and_critic_disagree' risk flag warrants LLM advisory attention. The data_granularity_score of 0.68 and machine_readability_score of 0.72 suggest the document may contain useful numeric summaries but is unlikely to provide the subnational (province/health-zone) granularity required by the collection spec. The independence_score of 0.90 is strong, indicating ECDC is not simply republishing DRC MoH verbatim, but this also means ECDC figures may diverge from primary DRC sources and introduce double-counting risk if used alongside WHO, Africa CDC, or INRB reports. The risk_penalty of 0.10 is modest but appropriate. Overall, this source is credible for contextual validation and cross-referencing but should not be the primary extraction source for DRC subnational case/death counts.

This source is a Facebook post from the account "cgtnafrica" — a social media page, not an official public health agency, international organization, or structured database. Despite the deterministic assessment assigning an authority_score of 0.88 (likely inflated by the CGTN Africa brand recognition) and a source_type label of "international_organization_report," the actual hosting domain is facebook.com, which is a social media platform with no editorial controls, no structured data, no versioning, and no verifiable provenance chain for epidemiological figures. The source_type label "international_organization_report" is a critical metadata mislabel — CGTN Africa is a state-affiliated broadcast media outlet, not an international public health organization. The post appears to be a media summary or repost of health official statements, not a primary or authoritative epidemiological report. Key structural deficiencies include: (1) no publisher metadata, (2) no snippet available for content verification, (3) social media platform with no data integrity guarantees, (4) low local_relevance_score (0.25) and low geographic_granularity_score (0.3), indicating the source likely lacks subnational or health-zone-level data required by the collection spec, (5) the query used targeted authoritative domains (who.int, africacdc.org, reliefweb.int) but this result resolved to facebook.com — a strong signal of query-result domain mismatch. The risk_penalty of 0.16 and the "screening_and_critic_disagree" flag further indicate internal inconsistency in the deterministic pipeline. The source should not be used as a primary or validation data source for structured epidemiological extraction. If any numeric claims are present in the post, they must be traced back to and verified against the original official source (e.g., DRC MoH, WHO, Africa CDC) before any data ingestion. Human review is recommended to adjudicate the source_type mislabel and confirm exclusion or downgrade.

This source is a Facebook post from Arise TV News — a broadcast media outlet — sharing what appears to be a summary of WHO-reported Mpox statistics for DRC in 2024. Several compounding credibility concerns apply:

1. **Domain mismatch vs. source_type**: The domain is `facebook.com` (a social media platform), but the source_type is tagged as `international_organization_report`. This is a significant metadata misclassification. The content may reference WHO data, but the source itself is a social media post by a news broadcaster, not an official WHO publication. This mismatch alone warrants a credibility downgrade and role reassignment.

2. **Secondary/tertiary provenance**: Even if Arise TV News accurately relays WHO figures, this is at minimum a second-hand report. The original WHO situation report or Disease Outbreak Notice (DON) is the authoritative source and should be sought directly. Using this Facebook post as a collection source risks introducing transcription errors, truncation, or loss of methodological context.

3. **Data granularity limitations**: The snippet references national-level aggregates (≥8,000 cases, 384 deaths for all of 2024). The collection task requires subnational granularity (province- and health-zone-level) for August 2024 specifically. A Facebook post headline is extremely unlikely to contain the required `subnational_location`, `locality`, `cases_confirmed`, `cases_probable`, `cases_suspected`, or `hospitalizations` fields at the needed resolution.

4. **Missing publisher field**: The publisher is null, which is anomalous even for a social media post — the page owner (Arise TV News) should be resolvable. This may indicate incomplete metadata harvesting.

5. **Temporal scope mismatch**: The figures cited (≥8,000 cases, 384 deaths) appear to be cumulative 2024 totals, not August 2024 monthly data. This does not align with the collection window of 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.

6. **`screening_and_critic_disagree` flag**: The deterministic assessment itself flags internal disagreement, which is a signal that this source warrants additional scrutiny before any role is finalized.

7. **PHEIC context risk**: During the August 2024 PHEIC declaration period, social media posts referencing WHO data are especially prone to selective quoting, outdated figures, or conflation of cumulative vs. period-specific counts.

**Advisory recommendation**: Downgrade role from `context` to `deprioritized` or `discard` for direct data collection purposes. The primary WHO source (WHO DON, WHO AFRO sitrep, or INRB bulletin) should be retrieved directly. This Facebook post may serve only as a breadcrumb to locate the original WHO report, not as a citable data source.

PHEIC CONTEXT: WHO declared mpox a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on 14 August 2024, driven substantially by the DRC clade Ib outbreak — expect elevated reporting volume, potential data revisions, and multiple overlapping sitreps during this window

CLADE SPECIFICITY: DRC August 2024 data involves both endemic clade I and the newly characterized clade Ib (associated with sexual transmission networks in eastern DRC, particularly South Kivu) — distinguish clade when reported
DATA COMPLETENESS: DRC surveillance infrastructure is resource-constrained; significant underreporting is expected, especially at health-zone and community levels
LANGUAGE: Primary official DRC sources are in French — query terms and source reading must accommodate French-language content ('cas', 'décès', 'flambée', 'bulletin épidémiologique', etc.)
TEMPORAL OVERLAP: August 2024 data may appear in reports dated September or October 2024 (retrospective sitreps) — do not restrict source search strictly to August publication dates

EXTRACTION MODEL WARNING (from task_input_warnings): extraction_record_model_still_hantavirus_named — verify that the extraction schema in use has been updated to Mpox-appropriate field names before ingestion; do not allow Hantavirus-specific fields to contaminate Mpox records

SOURCE DISCOVERY WARNING (from task_input_warnings): source_discovery_not_yet_disease_generic — source discovery pipeline may not yet be fully generalized; manually verify that Mpox-specific source categories (WHO DON, Africa CDC, INRB, DRC MoH) are included in the discovery scope
DOUBLE-COUNTING RISK: WHO, Africa CDC, and DRC MoH may report the same underlying data — cross-reference source chains and avoid double-counting when aggregating
SUBNATIONAL GRANULARITY: Prioritize province-level and health-zone-level data; national aggregates alone are insufficient for this collection task
EVIDENCE QUOTE REQUIREMENT: Every extracted record must include a verbatim evidence_quote from the source document supporting the numeric values recorded

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), WHO AFRO situation reports, and Africa CDC bulletins reporting Mpox cases and deaths in DRC for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON and Africa CDC are the highest-priority primary reporting channels for DRC Mpox during the August 2024 outbreak escalation period. These sources contain extractable confirmed, probable, suspected case counts and deaths at national and subnational level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique) and INRB epidemiological bulletins (bulletins épidémiologiques) for Mpox in DRC covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The DRC MoH and INRB are the national authoritative sources for subnational (province and health zone) Mpox surveillance data. French-language bulletins are the primary format and are essential for subnational_location and locality field extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Mpox situation reports and multi-country updates covering DRC for the period 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global Mpox sitreps published in August 2024 aggregate DRC-specific data and may include subnational breakdowns, clade I/Ib distinctions, and weekly case/death counts extractable for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (Global.health, Our World in Data, ProMED) that aggregate DRC Mpox case and death counts for August 2024 for cross-validation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be held back and used to validate extracted records from primary collection sources without leakage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ECDC rapid risk assessments or technical reports covering DRC Mpox clade I/Ib for August 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ECDC published technical assessments on DRC Mpox clade Ib in mid-2024 that include epidemiological summaries usable for validation of case and death counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and preprints describing DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology, case definitions, and surveillance methodology for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), clade classification, and count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify news and situation report sources (Reuters, AP, Reliefweb, OCHA) covering DRC Mpox outbreak in August 2024 for early signal detection and subnational location corroboration.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and humanitarian situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, subnational location names, and corroborating counts that support collection and help identify gaps in official reporting.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), unclear reporting periods, or mixed clade data for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: DRC Mpox reporting in August 2024 involved both clade I and clade Ib, cumulative and weekly counts, and national vs. subnational aggregations. Sources that do not clearly distinguish these dimensions require human adjudication.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: WHO AFRO, WHO HQ Disease Outbreak News, Africa CDC, DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique, Hygiène et Prévention), and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale) are the authoritative primary reporting agencies for DRC Mpox. These sources publish weekly and monthly epidemiological bulletins with subnational (province, health zone) case and death breakdowns, confirmed/probable/suspected case classifications, and clade I/Ib distinctions directly relevant to the August 2024 target window.

WHO global Mpox situation reports, ECDC rapid risk assessments, OCHA humanitarian situation reports, and Reliefweb updates provide independently compiled DRC Mpox data for August 2024. These serve as validation sources because they aggregate data from official DRC sources but are published independently, enabling cross-check of case and death counts.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints (PubMed, medRxiv, Lancet, NEJM, Eurosurveillance) on DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology published in 2024 provide case definitions, surveillance methodology context, and may contain extractable case/death data for the August 2024 period. Essential for interpreting count semantics and normalizing confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.

Structured public-health databases including Global.health line lists, Our World in Data Mpox tracker, WHO Mpox data repository, and ProMED archive provide machine-readable or structured DRC Mpox counts for August 2024. These are held back for validation to cross-check extracted records from primary collection sources.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC), humanitarian portals (Reliefweb, OCHA), and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Health Policy Watch) published DRC Mpox outbreak coverage in August 2024 coinciding with the WHO PHEIC declaration. These sources provide early outbreak signals, subnational location corroboration, and may cite official figures directly quotable as evidence.

iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_coverage_assessment: Iteration 1 surfaced strong candidate sources across international organizations (WHO, UNICEF, ECDC, CDC) and one INRB/ReliefWeb French-language sitrep. The UNICEF SitRep (20 Aug–1 Sep 2024) snippet contains a partial aggregate figure (20,015 suspected cases, 632 deaths as of week 35) but this is a year-to-date cumulative figure, not an August-only monthly total. The ReliefWeb sitrep No. 025 (29 Aug 2024) is the most directly relevant national source but only appeared as a title/URL — no numeric content was confirmed. WHO DON 2024-DON522 covers the DRC outbreak context but its snippet does not contain August 2024 case counts. The PMC article on Kokolo health zone (Kinshasa) covers August–November 2024 and could provide locality-level data. Africa CDC was not represented in the top results despite being a primary source for weekly African Mpox data. WHO AFRO external situation reports for August 2024 (sitrep nos. covering epi weeks 31–35) were not directly surfaced. Coverage is promising but incomplete for the target fields.
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment: High-trust sources identified: WHO DON (who.int), UNICEF SitRep (unicef.org), ReliefWeb-hosted DRC sitrep No. 025 (reliefweb.int, sourced from DRC Ministry of Health/INRB), ECDC (ecdc.europa.eu), INRB (inrb.cd), CDC HAN (cdc.gov), PMC peer-reviewed article (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov). Medium-trust: MSF/Doctors Without Borders (operational context, not primary surveillance data), NETEC (secondary summary). Low-trust: facebook.com posts (not usable as primary evidence). The facebook.com results should be excluded from evidence extraction. The ReliefWeb sitrep No. 025 and INRB result are the highest-priority targets for August 2024 subnational data.

selection_manifest.human_review_reason: The ECDC is a highly authoritative international public health body (authority_score=0.95), and this report is directly disease-relevant (disease_relevance_score=0.95) and timely (timeliness_score=0.95) for the August 2024 Mpox/clade I window. However, the deterministic model correctly penalizes this source on local and geographic granularity grounds (local_relevance_score=0.58; geographic_granularity_score=0.58): ECDC epidemiological updates on DRC Mpox are produced from a European surveillance perspective and typically aggregate or summarize DRC data rather than originating it. The source is therefore best suited to a 'context' role rather than primary 'collection'. The role_hint was 'collection' but both the deterministic role assignment and the source_role_final converge on 'context', and the 'screening_and_critic_disagree' risk flag warrants LLM advisory attention. The data_granularity_score of 0.68 and machine_readability_score of 0.72 suggest the document may contain useful numeric summaries but is unlikely to provide the subnational (province/health-zone) granularity required by the collection spec. The independence_score of 0.90 is strong, indicating ECDC is not simply republishing DRC MoH verbatim, but this also means ECDC figures may diverge from primary DRC sources and introduce double-counting risk if used alongside WHO, Africa CDC, or INRB reports. The risk_penalty of 0.10 is modest but appropriate. Overall, this source is credible for contextual validation and cross-referencing but should not be the primary extraction source for DRC subnational case/death counts.

This source is a Facebook post from the account "cgtnafrica" — a social media page, not an official public health agency, international organization, or structured database. Despite the deterministic assessment assigning an authority_score of 0.88 (likely inflated by the CGTN Africa brand recognition) and a source_type label of "international_organization_report," the actual hosting domain is facebook.com, which is a social media platform with no editorial controls, no structured data, no versioning, and no verifiable provenance chain for epidemiological figures. The source_type label "international_organization_report" is a critical metadata mislabel — CGTN Africa is a state-affiliated broadcast media outlet, not an international public health organization. The post appears to be a media summary or repost of health official statements, not a primary or authoritative epidemiological report. Key structural deficiencies include: (1) no publisher metadata, (2) no snippet available for content verification, (3) social media platform with no data integrity guarantees, (4) low local_relevance_score (0.25) and low geographic_granularity_score (0.3), indicating the source likely lacks subnational or health-zone-level data required by the collection spec, (5) the query used targeted authoritative domains (who.int, africacdc.org, reliefweb.int) but this result resolved to facebook.com — a strong signal of query-result domain mismatch. The risk_penalty of 0.16 and the "screening_and_critic_disagree" flag further indicate internal inconsistency in the deterministic pipeline. The source should not be used as a primary or validation data source for structured epidemiological extraction. If any numeric claims are present in the post, they must be traced back to and verified against the original official source (e.g., DRC MoH, WHO, Africa CDC) before any data ingestion. Human review is recommended to adjudicate the source_type mislabel and confirm exclusion or downgrade.

This source is a Facebook post from Arise TV News — a broadcast media outlet — sharing what appears to be a summary of WHO-reported Mpox statistics for DRC in 2024. Several compounding credibility concerns apply:

1. **Domain mismatch vs. source_type**: The domain is `facebook.com` (a social media platform), but the source_type is tagged as `international_organization_report`. This is a significant metadata misclassification. The content may reference WHO data, but the source itself is a social media post by a news broadcaster, not an official WHO publication. This mismatch alone warrants a credibility downgrade and role reassignment.

2. **Secondary/tertiary provenance**: Even if Arise TV News accurately relays WHO figures, this is at minimum a second-hand report. The original WHO situation report or Disease Outbreak Notice (DON) is the authoritative source and should be sought directly. Using this Facebook post as a collection source risks introducing transcription errors, truncation, or loss of methodological context.

3. **Data granularity limitations**: The snippet references national-level aggregates (≥8,000 cases, 384 deaths for all of 2024). The collection task requires subnational granularity (province- and health-zone-level) for August 2024 specifically. A Facebook post headline is extremely unlikely to contain the required `subnational_location`, `locality`, `cases_confirmed`, `cases_probable`, `cases_suspected`, or `hospitalizations` fields at the needed resolution.

4. **Missing publisher field**: The publisher is null, which is anomalous even for a social media post — the page owner (Arise TV News) should be resolvable. This may indicate incomplete metadata harvesting.

5. **Temporal scope mismatch**: The figures cited (≥8,000 cases, 384 deaths) appear to be cumulative 2024 totals, not August 2024 monthly data. This does not align with the collection window of 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.

6. **`screening_and_critic_disagree` flag**: The deterministic assessment itself flags internal disagreement, which is a signal that this source warrants additional scrutiny before any role is finalized.

7. **PHEIC context risk**: During the August 2024 PHEIC declaration period, social media posts referencing WHO data are especially prone to selective quoting, outdated figures, or conflation of cumulative vs. period-specific counts.

**Advisory recommendation**: Downgrade role from `context` to `deprioritized` or `discard` for direct data collection purposes. The primary WHO source (WHO DON, WHO AFRO sitrep, or INRB bulletin) should be retrieved directly. This Facebook post may serve only as a breadcrumb to locate the original WHO report, not as a citable data source.

metric_row_extraction_audit.row_quote: Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 38, published 28 September 2024 This situation report provides an update of the weekly mpox epidemiological situation in Africa, and the monthly global epidemiological situation. Highlights • This report provides an update on the mpox epidemiological situation in Africa as of 22 September 2024. A total of 6603 confirmed mpox cases, including 32 deaths have been reported across 15 African countries in 2024, with 402 confirmed cases and no deaths reported in the last week. The Democratic Republic of the Congo accounts for most cases (5621 cases, 25 deaths), followed by Burundi (696 cases, no deaths) and Nigeria (78 cases, no deaths). • All currently affected countries on the continent have reported new cases in the last six weeks, with Guinea reporting its first mpox case in the past month. • Testing challenges and delays in case confirmation persist in the Democratic Republic of the Congo persist, with 37% of suspected cases tested in 2024. Positivity among tested cases is around 55%. • In 2024, as of 22 September, 31 427 suspected cases, including 844 deaths (CFR 2.7%) have been reported in Africa, with 2085 new cases and 32 deaths in the last week. The Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Nigeria are reporting the most suspected cases. • In this report, the latest data received enabled a more detailed analysis of the national and subnational epidemiological situation for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and for Burundi. o In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, cases linked to clade Ib MPXV are driving outbreaks particularly in South Kivu province. 1 In some countries, suspected cases that undergo testing are not removed from the overall count of suspected cases, regardless of whether the test result is positive (confirmed case) or negative (discarded case). KEY FIGURES Reporting period: 01 January 2022 – 31 August 2024 Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number countries reporting cases Global 106 310 234 123 Reporting period: 01 January – 22 September 2024 Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reported suspected cases Number of deaths among suspected cases Africa 6 603 32 31 427 844 Democratic Republic of the Congo1 5 621 25 27 103 838 Burundi1 696 0 1879 0 Reporting period: last 6 weeks, 12 August – 22 September 2024 Africa 2 009 1 12 498 232 Democratic Republic of the Congo1 1 268 0 9 847 232 Burundi1 613 0 1 546 0 Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 2 o Mpox deaths are concentrated in the provinces of Equateur, Sankuru, Tshuapa, and Tshopo, with high case fatality in some areas. o In Burundi, since the start of the outbreak in July 2024, 35 of 49 (71%) districts are affected, with children under 5 years of age comprising about 30% of confirmed cases. Approximately 93% of suspected cases are tested, and testing positivity is around 40%. • On 19 September 2024, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) recommended extending the indication of Modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) vaccine to adolescents from 12 to 17 years of age. • This edition of the report outlines a research roadmap for mpox prepared by WHO and partners In this edition: • Situation overview • Epidemiological update o Situation in Africa o Focus on the Democratic Republic of the Congo o Focus on Burundi • Global operational updates • Special Focus: Mpox research roadmap • WHO mpox resources Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 3 Situation overview This report provides an update on the epidemiological situation for mpox in Africa (including countries in the WHO African Region and some countries of the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region), with data as of 22 September 2024. Recent global updates for mpox can also be found in the WHO mpox surveillance report. WHO conducted the latest global mpox rapid risk assessment in early August 2024. Based on information available at the time, the mpox risk was assessed as follows: • In the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighbouring countries: high. • In areas of the Democratic Republic of the Congo where mpox is endemic: high. • In Nigeria and other countries of West, Central and East Africa where mpox is endemic: moderate. • In all other countries in Africa and around the world: moderate (while in individual countries or regional bloc assessments may vary, and the risk may be assessed as low). Individual-level risk is largely dependent on individual factors such as exposure risk and immune status, regardless of geographic area, epidemiological context, biological sex, gender identity or sexual orientation. This situation update in Africa presents reported confirmed mpox cases and deaths,2 as described in the WHO case definitions published in the Surveillance, case investigation and contact tracing for mpox interim guidance. It also presents nationally reported suspected mpox cases, as defined by the countries that have reported them, to provide the reader with more information on epidemiological trends in countries with limitations in access to testing, such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Note: The indicator of suspected cases should be interpreted with caution, as these are recorded according to varying national case definitions, and in some countries, suspected cases that undergo testing are not removed from the overall count of suspected cases, regardless of whether the test result is positive (confirmed case) or negative (discarded case). In the absence of more detailed information, it is currently not possible to correctly subtract confirmed cases from the total number of suspected cases reported; therefore, the confirmed cases represent a subset of suspected cases. Definitions of suspected mpox cases for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Burundi can be found here. 2 For the WHO European region, both confirmed and probable cases are included within confirmed case counts and detailed case data. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 4 Epidemiological update Situation in Africa in 20243, 4 In 2024, and as of 22 September, 15 countries in Africa have reported 6603 confirmed mpox cases (see Figure 1, left), including 32 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] among confirmed cases of 0.5%). In the last week 402 new confirmed cases and no new deaths were reported. The three countries reporting the most cases in 2024 are the Democratic Republic of the Congo (5621 confirmed cases, 25 deaths), Burundi (696 confirmed cases, no deaths), and Nigeria (78 confirmed cases, no deaths). In addition to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, deaths among confirmed mpox cases in 2024 have been reported in South Africa (three), Cameroon (two), Central African Republic (one) and Cote d’Ivoire (one). Among the countries reporting mpox in 2024, all 15 countries have reported new confirmed cases within the past six weeks (see Figure 1, right). The six weeks refer to two mpox incubation periods of 21 days. In the past month, one country, Guinea, reported its first mpox case. Figure 1. Geographic distribution of confirmed mpox cases, by country, Africa, 2024 (left, 1 January – 22 September) and the last six weeks (right, 26 August – 22 September). Figure 2, showing the number of confirmed mpox cases in Africa by reporting country, indicates a continued rising trend of mpox in the continent. This is mainly driven by Burundi and a few provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, particularly South Kivu. Nevertheless, the epidemic curve in Figure 2 may underrepresent the epidemiological situation given the limited testing capacities in several African countries, especially in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where from January to September 2024 around 37% of suspected cases have been tested, with a test positivity of 54%. Challenges include absence or stockouts 3 On the African continent there are 47 Member States in the WHO African Region and seven in the Eastern Mediterranean Region. 4 Slight discrepancies in epidemiological data are expected between this report and the WHO Africa Regional Office, Regional Mpox Bulletin: 20 September 2024 due to different reporting dates. The Regional Mpox Bulletin is available in the following link: Mpox (monkeypox) | WHO | Regional Office for Africa Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 5 of sampling and testing supplies, difficulties in specimen referral in remote and underserved areas, collection of in appropriate or inadequate specimens, such as blood or samples taken in later stages of the disease, quality of the samples collected and delays between sampling and availability of laboratory results. Figure 2. Epidemic curve of reported confirmed mpox cases in Africa, by reporting country, 1 January 2024 – 22 September 2024 From 1 January to 22 September 2024, 31 166 suspected mpox cases and among these 844 deaths due to mpox (CFR 2.7%) were reported in Africa through syndromic surveillance systems which include tested and untested cases. (Figure 3) In the last week, 2 085 new suspected cases and 32 deaths were reported. The three countries reporting the most suspected mpox cases in 2024 are the Democratic Republic of the Congo (27 103 suspected cases, 838 deaths), Burundi (1879 cases, no deaths), and Nigeria (935 cases, no deaths). When compared with trends in confirmed cases, there has been a consistently rising trend in weekly reports of suspected cases (Figure 3) since May 2024, especially in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The trends in the number of reported cases in the last weeks of both epidemic curves should be interpreted with caution, given completeness and reporting delays. Figure 3. Epidemic curve of reported suspected mpox cases (tested and untested) in Africa, by reporting country, 1 January 2024 – 22 September 2024 Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 6 Focus on the Democratic Republic of the Congo In 2024, all provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have reported suspected mpox cases. Available sequencing data has identified clade Ib MPXV in three provinces, South Kivu, North Kivu and Kinshasa. Clade Ib MPXV was first identified in January 2024 in South Kivu, a province unaffected by mpox prior to September 2024; clade Ib MPXV is associated with a rapid rise in case reports in the province. MPXV clade Ib and clade Ia were found to be cocirculating in Kinshasa in July-August 2024.5 In 2024, the provinces reporting the highest number of suspected mpox cases are Equateur and South Kivu, followed by Sankuru, Sud Ubangi, Tshopo, Tshuapa and Mongala (Figure 4, left). The same provinces have also reported the highest number of confirmed mpox cases in 2024 (Figure 4, right). Trends in suspected cases reveal important differences between provinces6 – the number of weekly reported cases in Equateur is stable, with approximately 100 - 200 suspected cases reported per week, while the trend in South Kivu continues to rise with around 500 - 600 cases reported per week. Weekly reported cases are also increasing in Sankuru, Sud Ubangi, Tshopo, Tshuapa and Mongala. While the higher number of reported mpox cases may in part be attributable to strengthened surveillance, there is also evidence to support rising mpox transmission in the country in recent years.7 Figure 4. Global situation The mpox global situation update is provided monthly. For the latest information (as of August 2024) please refer to the following report: Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #37 - 22 September 2024 (who.int) 8 The first mpox cases were detected in Burundi in July 2024. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 9 Global operational updates The WHO health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience (HEPR) framework underpins both the Strategic Framework for enhancing prevention and control of mpox (2024-2027) and the current emergency response to the mpox Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Aligned with the HEPR framework, the WHO Global Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP) for mpox focuses on strengthening five core components—the 5Cs: 1. Emergency coordination: Efficient coordination for timely crisis response. 2. Collaborative surveillance: Real-time data integration for early threat detection. 3. Community protection: Engaging communities in prevention and resilience-building measures. 4. Safe and scalable care: Equipping health systems to provide essential care with scalable capacity. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures: Ensuring equitable distribution of medical countermeasures. This section provides updates on the WHO global mpox response as of 22 September 2024. 1. Emergency coordination • Through its Country Offices WHO is supporting Member States in operationalizing response plan guided by the Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP). Coordinating with Partners WHO is supporting national coordination structures including activated Incident Management Systems (IMS) in technical areas such as surveillance and epidemiological analysis, vaccination, infection prevention and control (IPC), risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), treatment and therapeutics, operation support and logistics (OSL), among others. On request of Member States, WHO AFRO Regional Office and headquarters have deployed experts to support response operations. • WHO is still working with relevant partners to design research activities for a better understanding of the outbreak and evidence-based strategies (refer to special focus below). 2. Collaborative surveillance • Epidemiological data on mpox updated weekly can be accessed on the WHO surveillance report here. • WHO updated the template transmission studies protocol to support mpox field investigations. • A webinar on the use of digital and analytics tools for mpox response was held on 24 September 2024. Countries shared their experience using Go.Data for mpox response. Analytical tools and initiatives highlighted included the Collaboratory epidemiological parameters for modelling and analysis, and software tools for addressing common analytics tasks. • An EPI-WIN webinar on collaborative surveillance for mpox was held on 26 September 2024. WHO and Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shared updates on current mpox global surveillance, the main activities to support countries with mpox surveillance, persisting challenges and an update of the current epidemiological situation. • WHO convened the Orthopoxvirus Laboratory Network to review and update interim guidance on diagnostic testing for monkeypox virus (MPXV). The upcoming update to this interim guidance shall include the latest guidance on MPXV near-point-of-care tests and antigen rapid diagnostic tests. • WHO and partners initiated the diagnostics workstream of the Access and Allocation Mechanism (AAM). 3. Community protection • Coordination for community protection continues, covering risk communication, RCCE and infodemic management; community IPC; water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH); home-based care; vaccination; border health and mass gatherings; and managing risks of transmission between animals and humans. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 10 Key multi-partner and civil society engagement and advocacy meetings were held in the reporting period: • The Community Protection Partners Network meeting held on 20 September 2024 focused on home-based care and community-based infection prevention and control, especially for low resource settings. • The informal community reference group of civil society organizations, networks and researchers was held on 20 September with representatives from 15 Countries from WHO AFRO, EURO and PAHO regions. Community representatives emphasized the importance of 1) ensuring that messages reach key populations, especially communities affected by HIV, and 2) community preparedness and involvement in the response to address complex layers of stigma and discrimination which hamper efforts to reach key populations and other marginalized groups. Special efforts are required to reach people with disabilities. • The Collective Service is an interagency initiative between IFRC, UNICEF, WHO, and GOARN for the coordinated delivery of RCCE for public health emergencies. A bi-monthly global call provides a platform for partners to share and hear updates on the global situation. 4. Safe and scalable care • A rapid assessment tool for IPC and WASH in health facilities has been shared with the African Regional Office and affected countries. This is being implemented in many health facilities in hotspot areas to identify opportunities for improvement in IPC practices and WASH services to ensure health workers and patients remain safe while receiving care. • Posters for health and care workers for putting on and removing PPE for mpox are available on the WHO website. Steps to put on PPE for mpox, Steps to remove PPE for mpox. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures Vaccines • On 19 September 2024, the European Medicines Agency recommended extending the indication of Modified vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) smallpox/mpox vaccine to include adolescents 12 to 17 years of age. • The WHO Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety met on 20 September to review available safety data on mpox vaccines and WHO protocols for safety monitoring. Diagnostics • In working towards emergency use listing of mpox diagnostics EUL, WHO is conducting a bridged assessment of 2 dossiers and expecting another dossier submission in coming days. • On 25 September 2024, WHO met with representatives from Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda and Tanzania to explore coordination on vaccine safety surveillance data and sharing of data. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 11 Special focus A coordinated research roadmap for monkeypox virus: Immediate research next steps to contribute to control the outbreak From 29-30 August, 2024, the Africa CDC, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), the United States National Institutes of Health (US NIH) and WHO held a scientific conference aimed at aligning research efforts with the practical needs of mpox outbreak control. In a comprehensive effort to synchronize research initiatives with the immediate requirements of mpox outbreak management, discussions emphasized collaboration, regulatory and ethics considerations, and national leadership. Over 2500 participants from affected countries and around the world— scientists, Member State representatives, public health professionals, funding agencies and private sector representatives— gathered to accelerate development of innovations to control the mpox epidemic. The meeting aimed to develop an emergency mpox research response agenda, enhance collaboration and partnerships, and outline key steps and timelines for addressing research gaps, emphasizing the leading role of affected countries and their researchers in shaping the research agenda. Key principles guiding the meeting included collaboration, leadership from affected regions, alignment with outbreak response goals, and a people-centered focus. There was consensus on the need for studies that 1) contribute to controlling the outbreak; 2) guide interventions so that those at the highest risk of infection are protected, promptly diagnosed, and receive optimal care; and 3) catalyze integration of research in each area of outbreak response, in a collaborative manner and with researchers and ministries of health of the affected countries in the driving seat. Ten immediate next steps for a coordinated Research Roadmap: 1. Obtain additional data on mpox transmission and epidemiology, including clinical outcomes and risk factors for severe disease. 2. Evaluate and deploy new rapid and sensitive diagnostic tests that detect all monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades and help with the differential diagnosis of diseases that can resemble mpox. 3. Define and implement all elements of an optimized clinical standard of care for all mpox patients. 4. Promote development of new therapeutics and evaluation of safety and efficacy of prioritized candidate therapeutics for mpox, in coordinated collaborative multicenter trials. 5. Conduct research on animal models and use animal models towards the determination of correlates of protection, and support research on immunoassays. 6. Define regulatory pathways for “next generation” medical countermeasures. 7. Facilitate availability of vaccines in areas with sustained human to human transmission as part of an integrated response, and promote generation of critical data regarding vaccine safety, performance and delivery strategies. 8. Use existing tools to incorporate Good Participatory Practices and community engagement in research including public health research. 9. Integrate research into outbreak response activities. 10. Embrace and expand opportunities for coordination and collaboration of all research initiatives with local authorities and research institutions, with researchers from affected countries and ministries of health at the centre of the response. A summary of these immediate next steps can be found here. A full research roadmap will follow. Highlights • This report provides an update on the mpox epidemiological situation in Africa as of 22 September 2024. A total of 6603 confirmed mpox cases, including 32 deaths have been reported across 15 African countries in 2024, with 402 confirmed cases and no deaths reported in the last week. The Democratic Republic of the Congo accounts for most cases (5621 cases, 25 deaths), followed by Burundi (696 cases, no deaths) and Nigeria (78 cases, no deaths). • All currently affected countries on the continent have reported new cases in the last six weeks, with Guinea reporting its first mpox case in the past month. • Testing challenges and delays in case confirmation persist in the Democratic Republic of the Congo persist, with 37% of suspected cases tested in 2024. Positivity among tested cases is around 55%. • In 2024, as of 22 September, 31 427 suspected cases, including 844 deaths (CFR 2.7%) have been reported in Africa, with 2085 new cases and 32 deaths in the last week.
